title: The Ark Is Captured
overview: Israel loses two battles to the Philistines, the sacred ark of God is captured, and the household of the priest Eli collapses in a single day.

parts.label: A first defeat (vv. 1-2)
parts.note: Samuel's word now reaches all Israel, but the text does not say the army asked him before going to war. Israel goes out against the Philistines, a powerful neighbouring people who dominated them at this time, and loses about four thousand men.

parts.label: Fetching the ark (vv. 3-4)
parts.note: The ark was a gold-covered chest holding the covenant tablets, topped by winged figures called cherubim, and was seen as the place of God's throne on earth. The leaders bring it from Shiloh hoping the LORD will go with them and save them, and it arrives with Eli's sons, whose wrongdoing chapter 2 said would bring ruin on Eli's family.

parts.label: Shouting and fear (vv. 5-9)
parts.note: Israel's huge cheer suggests they expect victory now, and the Philistines panic, saying a god has come into the camp. They link the ark with the plagues on Egypt, a story they seem to know only loosely, and urge each other to fight hard rather than become slaves to Israel.

parts.label: Total disaster (vv. 10-11)
parts.note: Israel is crushed, with the text counting thirty thousand dead, and the ark itself is taken. Eli's sons Hophni and Phinehas die, as had been foretold against Eli's family in chapter 2.

parts.label: Eli hears the news (vv. 12-18)
parts.note: A runner arrives with torn clothes and dust on his head, the usual signs of mourning, while Eli, blind and 98 years old, waits by the road fearing for the ark. It is at the mention of the ark that he falls backward and breaks his neck, after leading Israel forty years.

parts.label: Ichabod (vv. 19-22)
parts.note: Phinehas's wife goes into labour at the news and dies giving birth, not responding when the women tell her she has a son. She names him Ichabod, usually understood as "no glory" or "where is the glory?", because the ark's capture meant to her that God's glory had left Israel.

think: When something people count on as a sign of safety fails to protect them, what do you think that reveals about where their sense of security really came from?
